key_findings: Prolonged low-frequency (1 Hz x 150) primary afferent stimulation evokes non-Hebbian LTP at sensory synapses onto lamina I spinoparabrachial neurons in naive adult mouse SDH, independent of postsynaptic depolarization.
Non-Hebbian LTP requires postsynaptic NMDAR and mGluR5 activation and postsynaptic Ca2+, and reflects increased presynaptic glutamate release probability (reduced PPR).
EP2 antagonist PF 04418948 did not block non-Hebbian LTP, suggesting a retrograde messenger other than PGE2.
Prevalence and magnitude of non-Hebbian LTP are greater in spinoparabrachial projection neurons than in GABAergic or glutamatergic interneurons, and LTP occurs at Abeta, Adelta and C-fiber inputs.
